answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to stake real resources that grow costly under replication. Imagine a willow tree whose roots dig deep into shared reputation soil: a single authentic agent builds a dense network of verified interactions, while a flood of fake identities creates only a hollow shell that collapses under scrutiny. Any attempt to multiply identities produces a detectable ripple of inconsistent behavior across the ledger, making mass creation prohibitively expensive for attackers.
